il_d_spring_wall.blurb: Spring Wall is a sport crag inside Ferne Clyffe State Park near Goreville in far southern Illinois, reached by trail from the park's parking areas. It holds a dozen bolted routes on a tall, slightly overhanging face, set among mature trees and big boulders. This is a hard-climber's wall: the grades start at 5.11 and cluster in the 5.12s, with a handful of 5.13s and one route at 5.14 level, so there is little here for beginners. The stone is sandstone. It is one of several sport walls in the park, which makes it easy to pair with the neighbouring crags for a full day.

il_steelworkers_park.blurb: Steelworkers Park is an urban climbing wall on Chicago's far South Side lakefront, built from the concrete walls left by a former steel mill. The wall stands roughly 30 feet tall and is fitted with holds and bolts, with a few cracks that also carry bolts. Routes are short and mostly easy to moderate, running from the 5.7 range through the 5.10s with a single harder line, plus a few low problems from very easy up to about V4 near the base. It suits beginners, city climbers and anyone wanting a quick top-rope or bolted lap, though it is a manufactured wall rather than natural rock.
il_steelworkers_park.parking_note: Turn onto 87th Street from Lake Shore Drive and park inside the park; the wall is a very short walk from the cars.
